in_hebrew.name: חנריקוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name 'חנוך' (Hanokh) meaning 'grace, favour, kindness, The Hebrew suffix -יקוס (-yques) is derived from the Hebrew word 'יקוש' (yquesh) meaning 'to seek' or 'to find'. So, Henriques could be interpreted as 'one who finds grace' or 'one who is gracious and seeks grace'.

in_greek.name: Henrikos
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek name 'Henrikos' (Ἡνρικός), derived from 'Hen' (ἥν) meaning 'this' or 'the' and 'ríkos' (ρικός) meaning 'power' or 'lord'. So, Henriques could be interpreted as 'one who is the lord' or 'one who has the power' in Greek.

in_latin.name: Henricus
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin name 'Henricus' (Henrīcus), derived from 'Henrī' meaning 'ruler, leader' and 'ricus' meaning 'powerful, strong'. So, Henriques could be interpreted as 'strong ruler' or 'powerful leader' in Latin.
